Hon'ble Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 13.09.2024 Mac 182 of 2017 Smt. Kumari Bai vs Ajay Kumar Dewangan on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55246364/
1 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/Claimants, challenging the award dated 04.10.2016 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jashpur, District-Jashpur, CG (for short, 'Claims Tribunal'), in Claim Case- 16 of 2016, whereby learned Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.3,52,000/- as compensation to the claimants.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the claimants, who are wife, children and parents of the deceased-Harishankar, have filed claim case with the pleading that on 24.10.2015, when the deceased was going to his work in pick-up vehicle bearing registration No.CG 13 UE 2414 (hereafter,
referred to as 'offending vehicle'), by the rash and negligent driving of its Driver, NA1-Ajay Kumar Dewangan, deceased fell down on the road by which he received grievous injuries and on the way while taking him to the Hospital, he died.
Owner of the Offending vehicle was NA2-Murlidhar Yadav, and it is insured with NA3, Shriram General Insurance Company Limited.

3. At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 47 years and was earning Rs.12,000/- per month, from the work of Coolie, and thereby, claimants claimed Rs.48,05,000/- as compensation on various heads.

4. NA1, Driver, and NA2 Owner of the offending vehicle have denied the claim application and submitted that on the date of accident, the Driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective driving license Mac 182 of 2017 with him, and therefore, liability to pay compensation, if any, would be upon the Insurance Company.
5.

The Insurance Company has also contested the claim application and submitted that the deceased was an un-authorized passenger in the offending vehicle, and the accident occurred from the negligence of the diseased himself, and therefore, claimants are not entitled for any compensation.

It is also pleaded by the Insurance Company in its written statement, that Driver of the offending vehicle was not having any valid and effective driving license with him on the date of accident,
therefore, Insurance Company has no liability to pay any compensation to the claimants.

6. On the basis of pleadings made by the parties, learned Claims Tribunal has framed five issues and after recording the evidence and hearing them, passed the award on 04.10.2016, and has awarded Rs.3,52,000/- as compensation to the claimants.
7. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would submit that learned Claims Tribunal has awarded very meager amount towards compensation.

It has erred in considering the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- per month, whereas, the Tribunal should have taken the minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident, and should have awarded the amount of compensation suitably.
He would further submit that future prospects also have not been considered and very less Mac 182 of 2017 amount has been awarded on other conventional heads.
Therefore, the amount of compensation is to be enhanced suitably.

8. Learned Counsel for respondent-3 would support the impugned award and submit that learned claims Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased and has passed the impugned Smt. Kumari Bai vs Ajay Kumar Dewangan on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55246364/
2 award, which is just and proper, and needs no interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 9. Barring the oral evidence of the claimants, no document with regard to the profession, or income of the deceased has been filed.

However, looking to the date of accident, nature of job and minimum wage prevailing on the date of accident, this Court is of the view that Rs.5,800/- can safely be taken as monthly income of the deceased at the time of accident.

10. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:

sentences.text: Monthly
income of the diseased is being taken as Rs.5,800/- per month.

By adding 25% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.7,250/- {5800 + (5800 x 25/100)}.
Total yearly income of the deceased would be Rs.87,000/- (7250 x 12) Mac 182 of 2017
Out of the above total yearly income, 1/3 to be deducted towards personal expenditure of the deceased, as there are 5 claimants.
Now, actual yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.58,000/- {87000  (87000 x 1/3)}.

Deceased was aged about 47 years at the time of accident and the accident is of the year 2015, therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma (supra), multiplier of 13 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.7,54,000/-
(58000 x 13).
Rs.2,00,000/- towards filial and parental consortium, Funeral expenses- 15,000/-,
Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/- in view of Nanu Ram (supra), and 10% enhancement of the same in every three years

Now total compensation comes to Rs.10,53,000/- (754000 + 299000).
11.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.3,52,000/- already awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal, is now enhanced to Rs.10,53,000/-.
Thereby, the claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.7,01,000/- (1053000  352000).
Additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Monthly
income of the diseased is being taken as Rs.5,800/- per month.
By adding 25% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.7,250/- {5800 + (5800 x 25/100)}.
Total yearly income of the deceased would be Rs.87,000/- (7250 x 12) Mac 182 of 2017
Out of the above total yearly income, 1/3 to be deducted towards personal expenditure of the deceased, as there are 5 claimants.
Now, actual yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.58,000/- {87000  (87000 x 1/3)}.
Deceased was aged about 47 years at the time of accident and the accident is of the year 2015, therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma (supra), multiplier of 13 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.7,54,000/-
(58000 x 13).
Rs.2,00,000/- towards filial and parental consortium, Funeral expenses- 15,000/-,
Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/- in view of Nanu Ram (supra), and 10% enhancement of the same in every three years
comes to Rs.2,99,000/- {200000 + 15000 + 15000 +
69,000 (230000x 30/100)}.
Now total compensation comes to Rs.10,53,000/- (754000 + 299000).
11.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.3,52,000/- already awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal, is now enhanced to Rs.10,53,000/-.
Thereby, the claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.7,01,000/- (1053000  352000).
Additional amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.
The Insurance company is directed to pay compensation enhanced by this Court within 60 days from today.
On such deposit being made by the Insurance Company, Rs.5,00,000/- (Rs.1,00,000/-
to each of the claimants) shall be deposited in name of each appellant for a period of three years in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized bank.
Remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants equally, through Bank transaction/Account payee cheque.
